task_description: Add permissions snapshot integration testing to AWS CDK CLI - record IAM roles assumed and actions performed during integration tests, save as snapshots, and fail tests when permissions change

features.description: Create AWS SDK v3 middleware for permission tracking that intercepts API calls and captures IAM actions and assumed roles
steps: Create new package `@aws-cdk/integ-permissions-tracker` under `tools/@aws-cdk/` with TypeScript configuration
Implement `PermissionMiddleware` class that hooks into AWS SDK v3 middleware stack
Create `PermissionRecorder` class to collect and store captured permissions (service, action, role ARN, timestamp)
Implement STS AssumeRole tracking by intercepting `sts:AssumeRole` calls specifically
Add helper function to extract IAM action from SDK call (e.g., `s3:GetObject` from S3 GetObject command)
Create unit tests for middleware interception and permission extraction logic
Export public API for enabling/disabling tracking and retrieving recorded permissions
acceptance_criteria: Middleware correctly intercepts all AWS SDK v3 API calls
IAM actions are correctly derived from service and action names (e.g., `lambda:InvokeFunction`)
STS AssumeRole calls are tracked with the target role ARN
Multiple SDK clients can share the same recorder instance
Unit tests achieve >90% code coverage for the middleware module

features.description: Implement permission snapshot file format, serialization, and comparison utilities
steps: Define TypeScript interface `PermissionSnapshot` with schema for roles assumed and actions performed
Implement `PermissionSnapshotWriter` class for deterministic JSON serialization (sorted keys, normalized values)
Create `PermissionSnapshotReader` class to load and parse existing snapshot files
Implement `PermissionSnapshotComparator` for diffing actual vs expected permissions
Add utility functions for snapshot file naming convention (`integ.*.permissions.snapshot.json`)
Create clear diff output format showing added/removed roles and actions
Add unit tests for serialization, parsing, and comparison logic
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot format is human-readable JSON with clear structure
Serialization is deterministic - same permissions always produce identical output
Comparison correctly identifies added, removed, and unchanged permissions
Diff output is clear and actionable for developers
Snapshot files follow naming convention matching existing `.snapshot` directories

features.description: Integrate permission tracking into integration test runner and test execution workflow
steps: Modify `integration-test-runner.ts` to initialize permission tracker before test execution
Add environment variable or CLI flag `CDK_INTEG_PERMISSIONS_SNAPSHOT` to enable feature
Hook permission middleware into SDK clients used during `cdk deploy` and `cdk destroy`
Write permissions snapshot file after each test case completes
Store snapshot in test's `.snapshot` directory alongside existing artifacts
Add logic to skip permission tracking when running in dry-run or snapshot-only mode
Create integration test for the permission tracking feature itself
acceptance_criteria: Permission tracking can be enabled/disabled via configuration
Snapshot files are created in correct location with correct naming
Tracking does not significantly impact test execution performance (<5% overhead)
Feature works correctly with existing integ-runner commands and flags
Permissions are captured for both deployment and cleanup phases

features.description: Implement snapshot comparison, test assertions, and update workflow
steps: Add permission snapshot comparison to integ-runner test validation step
Implement clear error messages when permission snapshots differ from expected
Add `--update-permissions-snapshot` flag to update expected permissions on intentional changes
Create aggregation logic to combine permission snapshots across all tests
Implement GitHub Actions-friendly output format for CI/CD reporting
Add validation to prevent accidental permission changes without explicit acknowledgment
Create documentation for snapshot update workflow in error messages
acceptance_criteria: Tests fail with clear message when permissions change unexpectedly
Developers can update snapshots intentionally with explicit flag
CI/CD pipelines show clear diff when permission changes detected
Aggregated snapshot can serve as documentation of all required permissions
Workflow prevents accidental permission scope increases

features.description: Documentation updates for permission snapshot testing feature
steps: Add README.md to `@aws-cdk/integ-permissions-tracker` package explaining usage
Update `INTEGRATION_TESTS.md` with section on permission snapshot testing
Document snapshot file format and schema for external tooling integration
Add troubleshooting guide for common permission snapshot failures
Include example workflow for handling intentional permission changes
acceptance_criteria: Documentation clearly explains when and why permission snapshots change
Developers understand how to update snapshots when making intentional changes
Schema documentation enables external tooling to parse snapshot files
README includes code examples for enabling permission tracking
